doc: Cells confirmed, via live verification, to have NO real path forward -- the gap tool's own heuristics would otherwise keep re-flagging these as 'sourced-not-built'/'walled'/'no source known' on every regeneration, costing real investigation time to re-derive the same answer. Each entry needs: state, county (or null for every county in that state), column, reason (specific, falsifiable), confirmed_date, confidence ('high' = directly verified for this exact cell; 'medium' = inferred from a verified sibling/structural rule, not independently re-checked for every county it covers). gap_matrix.py's roll_up() checks this registry before finalizing each cell's gap_class and overrides to 'declined (<reason>)' when found -- never silently; the override is itself visible in the gap list so a human can challenge it. A declined entry is a claim, not a law: if new evidence contradicts one (the underlying platform adds a field, a law changes, a county switches vendors), remove or correct the entry and re-verify live before trusting the correction.

Its tax card's 'Land Market Value' vs 'Land Use Value' split looks like an ag-deferral field but live-checking 5 real parcel cards showed the split appears on ordinary RESIDENTIAL IMPROVED parcels too (not just FARM VACANT) -- it's a structural artifact of the acreage-valuation schedule (any parcel with a Gross Acres land record gets both numbers), not an ag-rollback flag. Wiring TOTBDGVAL as vacant_lot here would mis-flag real improved homes. Would need Florence's personal-property/mobile-home tax roll (a different, unbuilt source) to fix, not a reuse of this field.

South Carolina marriage licenses are issued and recorded by the county PROBATE COURT, never the Register of Deeds, statewide (state law, not county discretion) -- confirmed directly for Sumter (live-pulled its full 182-code CountyFusion/GovOS instrument-type tree: zero marriage-related codes) and corroborated by SCDHEC + Sumter's own Probate Court page. This is structurally different from NC, where RODs DO record marriage licenses (why the Johnston NC EagleWeb sweep worked). This project's ROD-platform infrastructure (sc_countyfusion.py, kofile.py, publicsearch.py, etc.) cannot reach Probate Court records at all -- a different county office entirely, not a missing filter. DIRECTLY verified only for Sumter; HIGH confidence it generalizes (state law), but not independently re-checked county-by-county.

NC tax-foreclosure sales are JUDICIAL (G.S. 105-374 in rem, or power-of-sale under G.S. 45-21.31 for mortgage-style tax foreclosures); any excess-over-debt proceeds are deposited with the CLERK OF SUPERIOR COURT inside that specific foreclosure special-proceeding's own case file, not published by the county tax office as a roster. Claiming requires a motion/petition referencing that case number (G.S. 45-21.31/105-374(q)); there is no county-wide or statewide published list of who has surplus -- confirmed independently two ways: (1) this repo's own gap_matrix.py Spec for this column already carries the ambiguity note 'SC counties publish excess-funds lists; NC clerks hold surplus without a published list', and (2) fresh 2026-11-10 web research (NC probate/estate-law firm Q&A content, a dozen+ independent articles) converges on the same claim-by-petition-to-the-case-file process with no published roster. After ~1 year unclaimed, money can migrate to the NC State Treasurer's generic Unclaimed Property Division (116B-62) -- a DIFFERENT, non-tax-sale-specific statewide database (bank accounts, uncashed checks, etc.), not a fix for this column; scraping it would need heavy filtering and is a separate future signal, not this one. This makes the 101 NC rows the gap matrix flags 'sourced-not-built' for lt_tax_sale_overage a heuristic false-positive (the matrix treats 'county has SOME tax source in county_records_matrix.json' as 'sourced' for every tax-family column, including this one, without checking that source actually publishes an overage list). Verified directly against the structural rule (judicial-foreclosure routing), not independently re-checked clerk-by-clerk for all 100 NC counties -- a county-specific override still wins if one clerk turns out to publish a list anyway.

No post-Helene parcel-level damage-assessment GIS layer exists or will exist here, even though Mecklenburg sits inside the broad ~71-county FEMA IA footprint (storm_scope). 2026-10-29 session found Mecklenburg's only logged tornado was EF-0 (negligible) via NOAA Storm Events + the state's own Helene damage briefing, but never implemented the override -- this session (2026-11-16) independently re-confirmed via FEMA OpenFEMA HousingAssistanceOwners/Renters per-household inspected-damage data for DR-4827: Mecklenburg averages $810 FEMA-inspected damage per inspected home (5,309 inspections), only 39 homes assessed above $30k, 8 max-grant recipients -- an order of magnitude below the counties this column's own producer (enrichment_helene_damage.py) already covers (Henderson: avg $4,184/home, 170 >$30k, 299 max grants; Buncombe: avg $2,840/home, 367 >$30k, 617 max grants). NOAA Storm Events' only Helene-week (2024-09-24..10-03) entries for Mecklenburg are a Flash Flood and a county-wide Tropical Storm wind estimate, no tornado, no structural-damage narrative. Real catastrophic structural damage -- the kind that drives a county to run and publish a parcel-level ATC-45 damage survey -- never happened here.

The federal IA registration here reflects generic storm-adjacent hardship, not structural damage. No county/city post-Helene parcel-level damage-assessment GIS layer exists or will exist here.

The Description-text signal genuinely does not exist on this vendor; this is not the same silent-gap bug class as qPayBill.

This vendor (ustaxdata.com, enrichment_ustaxdata_tax_search.py) has no present-use/land-use-deferral field of any kind -- already directly checked and documented in that module's own docstring, independent of this session: every row's 'Asset Description' cell reads the literal static placeholder '> CONTACT COUNTY FOR' on EVERY year and EVERY county tried (confirmed live 2026-10-16, not a fetch error), so there is no per-bill descriptive text at all for a '<year> ROLLBACK TAX...'-style marker (the qPayBill-vendor signal this sweep found 2026-11-05) to ever appear in. The summary table has no dollar amount either (that lives one click deeper, on a separate per-bill page this module already reads for tax_owed, which also carries no use-value split). Structurally weaker than a vendor that has real but merely-unexploited Description text -- here the field itself is dead on arrival.

Same ustaxdata.com vendor limitation as Robeson (see that entry -- the 'Asset Description' placeholder is vendor-wide, not county-specific). We are experiencing technical difficulties' (HTTP 200, not a bill) per enrichment_ustaxdata_tax_search.py's own docstring -- a pre-existing condition on the county's own server, not something this project caused, and not independently re-checked here as still current.

Granville is the SAME bttaxpayerportal/ITSPublic vendor as the Anson entry above (nc_its_public_tax.py PORTALS['Granville'], just hosted on the county's own domain tax.granvillecounty.org rather than the shared bttaxpayerportal.com name, which is why it did not group with the other 6 by hostname). The 'no value/use-split field in TaxBillSearch's own column set' argument is a PLATFORM-level fact (re-confirmed this session by reading parse_row_cols()/parse_description_cols() directly, not per-tenant), so it applies here unchanged. The Description-text live check (2 years, 7,386 rows, zero 'ROLLBACK' hits) was run directly against Anson/Yadkin/Caswell/Jones/Graham/Alleghany, NOT against Granville's own tenant -- kept at 'medium' confidence rather than 'high' for that reason; a county-specific live recheck would raise it.
